statements.impact_statement: GHSA-6v7p-g79w-8964 (CVE-2026-57585, PYSEC-2026-3625): in msgpack for Python before 1.2.1, reusing a streaming Unpacker after it has raised an error lets the C extension resume from a corrupt parser state, read out of bounds and crash the process with SIGSEGV, a denial of service when untrusted input is unpacked. The fix, https://github.com/msgpack/msgpack-python/commit/2c56ddb5d0025ed481d962c0f5d62d19dec7476d, released in https://github.com/msgpack/msgpack-python/releases/tag/v1.2.1, changes only the C extension's sources, msgpack/_unpacker.pyx and msgpack/unpack_template.h, so that the parser state is cleared after a failure; it does not touch the pure-Python implementation in msgpack/fallback.py. Advisory: https://github.com/msgpack/msgpack-python/security/advisories/GHSA-6v7p-g79w-8964. We read every k8s-sidecar package published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository as of 2026-11-28: 21 builds, 2.10.1-r0 to the current 2.14.3-r7, each for x86_64 and aarch64. Each package was checked against its index checksum. We walked every file in each package, including the members of python-dateutil's zoneinfo tarball, the only archive file, which the builds before 2.14.1-r2 carry; both architectures agree for every build. The only msgpack in any build is the copy pip vendors, /usr/lib/k8s-sidecar/.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/pip/_vendor/msgpack (msgpack 1.1.2, which pip's vendor.txt also pins), in builds 2.10.1-r0 to 2.14.1-r1. It holds __init__.py, exceptions.py, ext.py, fallback.py and COPYING, with no compiled _cmsgpack extension module, so its __init__.py falls back to the pure-Python Packer and Unpacker in fallback.py. No build contains msgpack's C extension module, _unpacker.pyx or unpack_template.h, and no ELF file in any build sits under a msgpack directory. From 2.14.1-r2 pip, and with it msgpack, is no longer in the package. Debian tracks this CVE against its own python-msgpack package (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-57585), which is not part of this owner.
